data.body:
rebar-debug Phase 1 RCA (fast path, confirmed).

Mechanism: `_check_work_landed` unconditionally calls `_referencing_commits` before either landing check (`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:219`). `_referencing_commits` reads the complete code-repo log and resolves every unique historical ticket reference (`:326-345`). Only afterward does `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` compute the accepted ticket/descendant impact union and return when it is empty (`:283-285`). Therefore a no-impact close performs repository-history × tracker-resolution work whose result cannot affect either check.

Proof and rivals: the report captured execution inside `resolve_ticket_id -> _scan_alias -> json.load` during the five-minute close. Static control-flow confirms the scan precedes the empty-union guard. An empty accepted-scope union implies the current ticket’s own `file_impact` is also empty, so the first check cannot raise; the second already returns. A ticket-only guard was rejected because accepted descendant impact must retain referencing-commit credit.

Legitimacy: defect. Existing `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` explicitly defines an empty union as out of scope, while the current ordering performs discarded work and violates the close precheck’s deterministic/cheap-gate expectation.

Caller/safety sweep: `_check_work_landed` has one internal caller at `close_precheck.py:635`; `_union_file_impact` already defines the correct ticket+descendant scope. Expected behavior is an early return only when that union is empty. No caller behaviorally depends on the discarded scan; impact-present, descendant-credit, administrative disposition, force, and completion-verifier paths remain on the existing checks. Phase 2 is unlocked.
